usage_pattern: Pass as the `backend=` kwarg: `create_qulacs_vector_sampler(seed, backend=MPI_BACKEND)`. Requires a power-of-two MPI process count and at least log2(size)+2 qubits; density-matrix, noise-simulator, and marginal-probability paths raise RuntimeError.
benefit: Distributes the state vector across MPI ranks so each process only holds its local slice, enabling larger qubit counts than fit in one process's memory.

usage_pattern: Standalone alternative factory (not a `backend=` kwarg) - call directly in place of `create_qulacs_vector_sampler`. Concurrent and multi-node variants also exist: `create_cuquantum_vector_concurrent_sampler`, `create_cuquantum_mnode_vector_sampler`.
benefit: GPU-accelerated statevector simulation via NVIDIA cuStateVec. `n_global_qubits > 0` enables multi-GPU simulation across 2**n_global_qubits GPUs.

usage_pattern: Standalone alternative factory - import replaces the OSS import, call directly with `backend=`, `contraction_strategy=`, and `max_bond_dimension=`/`max_truncation_err=`.
benefit: Contracts via time-evolving block decimation (TEBD) to keep the bond dimension bounded, trading exactness for scaling to more qubits than exact tensor-network contraction.

usage_pattern: Call directly; no OSS equivalent exists.
benefit: Efficiently simulates noisy quantum circuits using MPS and Pauli Transfer Matrix (PTM) representations.

usage_pattern: Standalone alternative factory for periodic (k-point) active spaces - import replaces the OSS import; internally delegates to the OSS function after summing active-space electrons/orbitals across k-points.
benefit: Extends the molecular Hamiltonian mapper to periodic/crystalline (k-point) active spaces, which the OSS function alone doesn't model.

usage_pattern: Call directly; composes the OSS `create_parameter_shift_gradient_estimator` and `create_parameter_shift_hessian_estimator` factories into one higher-level analytic energy-hessian estimator.
benefit: Implements the analytic energy-derivative formulae of Mitarai et al. (2020, Phys. Rev. Research 2, 013129), avoiding costly finite-difference Hessians.

usage_pattern: Call directly: `qsci(hamiltonian, approx_states, sampler, total_shots, backend=QSCI_GPU_BACKEND)`. `backend=` swaps between `QSCI_CPU_BACKEND` (default) and `quri_parts.plus.algo.eigensolver.qsci_gpu.QSCI_GPU_BACKEND`.
benefit: GPU backend accelerates truncated-Hamiltonian construction for larger active spaces. No OSS QSCI implementation exists.

usage_pattern: Import the relevant submodule directly, e.g. `from quri_algo.plus.circuit_lib.lcu import SELECT, LCU, QROM`. This is the current, maintained home for qsub-based FTQC circuit building blocks - `quri_parts.plus.qsub.lib.*` is deprecated (emits FutureWarning) in favor of this.
benefit: Fault-tolerant/qsub-level circuit-construction building blocks (SELECT/PREPARE/QROM, adders, amplitude-amplification, reflections) with no OSS counterpart.

usage_pattern: Pass as the `vm_backend=` kwarg: `VM(vm_backend=BraketDeviceBackend(aws_device))`. Constructor also takes `simulate=True` for a noisy-simulation mode using the real device's noise model and native gate transpiler.
benefit: Runs VM.sample/.analyze/.transpile against a real AWS Braket cloud device instead of an idealized logical-circuit simulator; wraps `generate_device_property` and the OSS `quri_parts.braket` sampling backend.

usage_pattern: Pass as the `vm_backend=` kwarg: `VM(vm_backend=QiskitDeviceBackend(ibm_backend))`. Constructor also takes `simulate=True` for a noisy-simulation mode using the real device's noise model and native gate transpiler.
benefit: Runs VM.sample/.analyze/.transpile against a real IBM Quantum backend instead of an idealized logical-circuit simulator; wraps `generate_device_property` and the OSS `quri_parts.qiskit` sampling backend.
